rawScoringGuide:
Consider the differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{3 x^{2}}{e^{2 y}}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find a solution \(y=f(x)\) to the differential equation satisfying \(f(0)=\frac{1}{2}\).
\item[(b)] Find the domain and range of the function \(f\) found in part (a).
\item[(a)] \(e^{2 y} d y=3 x^{2} d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{2} e^{2 y}=x^{3}+C_{1} \\
& e^{2 y}=2 x^{3}+C \\
& y=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(2 x^{3}+C\right) \\
& \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2} \ln (0+C) ; \quad C=e \\
& y=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(2 x^{3}+e\right)
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] Domain: \(2 x^{3}+e>0\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& x^{3}>-\frac{1}{2} e \\
& x>\left(-\frac{1}{2} e\right)^{1 / 3}=-\left(\frac{1}{2} e\right)^{1 / 3}
\end{aligned}
\]
Range: \(-\infty<y<\infty\)
\end{itemize}
\(6 \begin{cases}1: & \text { separates variables } \\ 1: & \text { antiderivative of } d y \text { term } \\ 1: & \text { antiderivative of } d x \text { term } \\ 1: & \text { constant of integration } \\ 1: & \text { uses initial condition } f(0)=\frac{1}{2} \\ 1: & \text { solves for } y\end{cases}\)
Note: 0/1 if \(y\) is not a logarithmic function of \(x\)
Note: \(\max 3 / 6\) [1-1-1-0-0-0] if no constant of integration
Note: 0/6 if no separation of variables

Note: \(0 / 3\) if \(y\) is not a logarithmic function of \(x\)
